tables.title: Blob creation steps for modular exponentiation (CCOP = 0b01000100)
tables.text: Table 194, "Blob creation steps for modular exponentiation (CCOP = 0b01000100)", in section 25.5.4 (RSA modular exponentiation) on page 765. Columns: OPSTEP, inM OPDKEA, iGn CSMAPEHS, Coupling or chaining operations, End-step (1)event, CPU action in step. 11 data row(s). Notes: 1. The application must clear and/or perform described event for CCB to automatically go to the next step.; 2. Once START bit is set SAES is reset, and OPERR linked to SAES are deactivated. Also when.

rows:
–Enable the PKA in the correct mode, writing in PKA_CR 
MODE= 0x3 and EN=1 (repeat if EN bit stays clear). Wait 
for INITOK=1 in PKA_SR.
–Optionally decrypt blob encryption key in the SAES, 
usingDHUK in 256-bit wrapped key mode.
–Set up AES-GCM in 256-bit encryption mode with DHUK 
or the decrypted key in register (if applicable).
–Write a constant K as operand A in the PKA RAM.

–Complete GCM initialization in encryption mode. 
SAES_IVR1 to 3 registers are loaded with randoms.
–Read back blob IV in SAES_IVR registers.

Write protected modular exponentiation parameters (PKA 
mode 0x3) in the PKA RAM, clearing CCF flags in the SAES 
triggered after each 2x32-bit write.

–Read incrementallye from the PKA (writing 0xCCB magic 
numbers), and runs AES encryption rounds.
–Read encrypted e in SAES_DOUTR. 
–Repeat for each 16 bytes block of data.

–Read incrementally phi from the PKA (writing 0xCCB 
magic numbers), and run AES encryption rounds.
–Read encrypted phi in SAES_DOUTR. 
–Repeat for each 16 bytes block of data

–Complete GCM final.
–Read reference tag in the SAES.
–Start the operation in PKA setting START bit in PKA_CR.
For the first two steps keep the SAES enabled (EN bit set).
The PKA computes the operation, PKA RAM is read as 0

e–Read the reference modular exponentiation K mod n in 
PKA RAM, and save it in SRAM to verify the new blob.
–Set IPRST in CCB

Clear the IPRST bit in CCB when CCB_BUSY and OPSTEP 
are cleared in CCB_SR.
notes: 1. The application must clear and/or perform described event for CCB to automatically go to the next step.
2. Once START bit is set SAES is reset, and OPERR linked to SAES are deactivated. Also when START bit is set, CCB sets OPSTEP to 0x19 after a few cycles.
3. SAES cannot be used for any operations, for security reasons.
